text: Girlfriends is an American situation comedy that aired for eight seasons, totaling 172 episodes, with its first six seasons on UPN and the final two on The CW. The series premiered on September 11, 2000, and concluded on February 11, 2008. Joan Clayton (played by Tracee Ellis Ross) is nearly 30, close to becoming a junior partner at her law firm, and has a strong friend circle. She hires Maya Wilkes (Golden Brooks) as her assistant and has been friends with colleague William (Reggie Hayes) for over three months. Joan is frustrated that she hasn't had a romantic partner in a year and believes she should be married by now. Her friends, the egotistical Toni Childs (Leslie Silva) and the lazy 27-year-old college student Lynn (Christina Cox), help cheer her up and get her a man, with Toni referring to Maya as "ghetto." Joan and William compete for a senior partner position, only to be shocked when the firm hires Sharon Upton Farley (Anne-Marie Johnson) as an outsider. They plan to protest by walking out, but only one of them actually does. Meanwhile, Lynn and Maya assist Toni in dealing with her fears after Todd asks her to take an HIV test. Joan and William confront Toni over her jealousy and negative attitude about her wedding, especially when Toni announces that Reesie Jackson, her college roommate, will be a bridesmaid. Reesie reveals that Brian, her husband and Joan’s ex-boyfriend, gave her AIDS. Lynn convinces Toni to visit Virginia to seek Sandy’s help before a grant presentation for her AIDS documentary; during the trip, Lynn meets her grandmother and learns a shocking secret about Sandy’s health. After discovering William’s new earnings, Maya tries to become his assistant to improve her salary and return to school, but William only agrees if Joan approves. Toni’s twin brother Antoine visits for a weekend with Maya, but becomes unsettling when he declares his love and says he won’t return to Boston; when she rejects him, he locks himself in the bathroom and refuses to leave. William orders Lynn to leave his house and continually sabotages her attempts to find a roommate. Toni agrees to help Joan clean out her house, but insists that Joan’s love life is what needs to be eliminated. Joan’s cousin Melanie Barnett (Tia Mowry), an aspiring med student, decides to abandon her medical career to pursue a professional athletic career. Maya moves into her new home, Toni and Todd attempt to reach a settlement, William pursues Monica, Joan attends an A-list party where she makes a dramatic mistake, and Lynn writes a song reflecting on the group’s growing distance. Concerned about William’s emotional state after his breakup with Monica, Maya, Joan, and Lynn travel to Chicago to convince Monica to reunite with William. Upon arrival, they learn Monica has been cut off from her family fortune, so Joan offers her a job at the J-Spot. William is initially thrilled when Monica returns, but she later demands half of what he earned during their relationship. Joan unexpectedly proposes to Aaron, but when he mishears his response, she concludes the relationship is over and walks away. Meanwhile, Maya and Darnell find their dream house, but when Darnell gets the chance to buy the garage, he must decide which purchase to make.
